title: Slow English Podcast #344: 20 Easy Facts About Iceland

sentences.text: Hello everyone. My name is Amelia. Welcome to the Slow English Podcast. I am very happy you are here today.
Today we will learn about a beautiful country. The country is Iceland. We will talk about 20 easy facts.
I will speak slowly. Take your time. Listen, relax and enjoy learning English. Let's begin.
Fact 1. Iceland is an island country. Iceland is an island in the North Atlantic Ocean.
It is between Europe and North America. The country is not very big, but it is very beautiful.
Many people dream of visiting Iceland one day. The island is famous for its amazing nature.
Every year millions of visitors come to see it. Fact 2. The capital city is Reykjavik.
Reykjavik is the capital and the largest city in Iceland. Most people in Iceland live in or near Reykjavik.
The city is clean, modern and peaceful. There are many colorful houses. There are museums, restaurants, parks and shops.
Even though it is the biggest city in Iceland, it is much smaller than cities like London or Paris.
People enjoy walking around the city. The air is fresh and the streets are quiet.
Fact 3. Iceland has a small population. About 400,000 people live in Iceland. That is fewer people than many cities around the world.
Because the population is small, there is a lot of open space. You can drive for a long time and see only mountains, rivers and fields.
Many people enjoy this peaceful lifestyle. Fact 4. Iceland is called the land of fire and ice.
This is one of Iceland's most famous nicknames. The country has many volcanoes. It also has many glaciers.
A volcano is full of hot lava. A glacier is made of ice. It is amazing that fire and ice can exist in the same country.
This makes Iceland one of the most interesting places on Earth.
Fact 5. Iceland has many active volcanoes. There are more than 100 volcanoes in Iceland. Some volcanoes are active.
Sometimes they erupt. When a volcano erupts, hot lava comes out of the ground.
Scientists watch the volcanoes carefully. Even though volcanoes can be dangerous, they also create beautiful landscapes.
Fact 6. Iceland has beautiful glaciers. About 10% of Iceland is covered with glaciers. Some glaciers are very large.
People visit them all year. Visitors can walk on the ice with special guides.
Glaciers are very old. Some of the ice is thousands of years old. They are one of Iceland's greatest natural treasures.
Fact 7. Iceland has hundreds of waterfalls. Waterfalls are everywhere in Iceland. Some are tall. Some are wide.
Some are hidden between mountains. One famous waterfall is Gullfoss. Another famous waterfall is Scogafoss.
Many visitors say Iceland has some of the most beautiful waterfalls in the world.
Fact 8. Hot Springs are everywhere. The ground under Iceland is very hot. Because of this, hot water comes from the ground.
These places are called Hot Springs. People love swimming in warm water. One famous place is the Blue Lagoon.
People visit it in every season. Even when snow is falling, the water stays warm.
Fact 9. Iceland uses clean energy. Most homes in Iceland use geothermal energy.
This energy comes from the heat inside the earth. The country also uses water to make electricity.
This is called hydroelectric power. Because of these natural resources, Iceland produces a lot of clean energy.
Many people around the world admire this.
Fact 10. Summer days are very long. In June, the sun stays in the sky for almost 24 hours.
This is called the Midnight Sun. People can walk outside late at night. Children can still play in the evening.
It feels strange for many visitors because it never becomes completely dark.
Fact 11. Winter nights are very long. Winter is very different. The days become short.
Sometimes the sun shines for only a few hours. People use lights inside their homes.
Even though winter is dark, it is also beautiful. Snow covers the mountains and fields.
Fact 12. Iceland is famous for the Northern Lights. Many people visit Iceland to see the Northern Lights.
The lights move across the night sky. They are usually green, but they can also be purple, pink or white.
People wait outside on cold nights to watch this amazing natural show. Seeing the Northern Lights is a dream for many travelers.
Fact 13. Iceland has no wild snakes. There are no wild snakes in Iceland. There are also no wild monkeys.
Many people are surprised by this fact. The cold climate makes it difficult for these animals to live there.
This makes Iceland different from many other countries. Fact 14. There are more sheep than people.
They walk freely in the fields and mountains. They eat fresh grass. In autumn, farmers bring them back home.
Sheep are an important part of Icelandic life. Fact 15. Icelandic horses are special.
The Icelandic horses are famous around the world. These horses are small but very strong.
They are friendly and calm. They can walk in a special way called the tilt. This walk is very smooth and comfortable.
Many visitors enjoy riding Icelandic horses. Fact 16. Fishing is very important. The ocean is an important part of Iceland.
Many people work in fishing. Fish is one of the country's biggest exports. Fresh seafood is common in restaurants.
People eat salmon, cod and many other kinds of fish. Fishing has been important in Iceland for hundreds of years.
Fact 17. Iceland has many interesting animals. You can see puffins in Iceland.
Puffins are small birds with colorful beaks. Many people visit Iceland just to see them.
You can also see whales in the ocean. Whale watching is a popular activity.
Sometimes people also see seals resting near the coast. Fact 18. Icelandic is the official language.
People in Iceland speak Icelandic. It is an old language. Many words are similar to the language used by the Vikings many centuries ago.
Most Icelanders also speak English very well. Because of this, visitors can communicate easily.
Fact 19. Iceland is one of the safest countries in the world. People often say Iceland is very safe.
Crime is low. People trust each other. Children often walk to school safely.
Visitors usually feel comfortable while traveling around the country.
This peaceful lifestyle is one reason many people love Iceland.
Fact 20. Iceland is a wonderful place to visit. Iceland has volcanoes, glaciers, waterfalls, mountains,
black sand beaches, hot springs and beautiful animals. It is full of natural beauty.
Every season offers something special. Some people visit in summer to enjoy the midnight sun.
Others come in winter to see the northern lights.
No matter when you visit, Iceland is a country full of amazing experiences.
Keep listening, keep practicing and keep enjoying English.
